title: A Dy4 Cubane: A New Member in the Single-Molecule Toroics Family

synthesis.procedure: BppdH (0.226 g, 1 mmol) and 2-picolinic acid (PaH, 0.061 g, 0.50 mmol) were added to DyCl3·6H2O (0.186 g, 0.5 mmol) previously dissolved in 3 mL MeOH. NEt3 (0.26 mL, 2 mmol) was then added dropwise, forming a yellow solution. After stirring for 1 h, the mixture was cooled at 5 °C for 48 h, affording small yellow crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction.
synthesis.temperature: stirred at unspecified ambient temperature, then cooled at 5 °C
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution synthesis followed by cooling crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: After cooling at 5 °C for 48 h, small yellow crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction formed.

properties.summary: The Dy4 cubane is a 3D single-molecule toroic (3D-SMT): χMT at room temperature is 52.1 cm3 K mol−1 (vs 56.6 expected for four DyIII), collapsing to 2.5 cm3 K mol−1 at 500 mK, with χM showing a rounded maximum at 2 K and an S-shaped magnetization curve saturating at 19.2 μB, consistent with a non-magnetic ground state. Fitted exchange couplings J1 = −0.27 cm−1 and J2 = −0.09 cm−1 stabilize a near-nonmagnetic toroidal ground doublet (effective g ≈ 0.46; strictly diamagnetic in a Td-symmetrized model). Frequency-dependent ac susceptibility between 2–11 K in zero dc field indicates slow magnetic relaxation, with thermally activated behavior at high T becoming thermally independent below 4 K; in-field χM′ at 2 K shows maxima at 2.8 and 4 kOe corresponding to calculated level crossings.
